parameters.name: repos

schema.description:
The environment's full list of repositories, replacing the
current list. It follows the same rules as `repos` on
POST /v1/environments. Send `environmentJson` with it, because a
repository change saves the whole configuration; `repos` without
`environmentJson` returns `400 validation_error`. To keep the
current configuration, send the `environmentJson` from
GET /v1/environments/{id}.

Only environments with two or more repositories can change them,
and they must keep at least two. Sending the current list
unchanged doesn't count as a change. Otherwise an environment
without repositories, a single-repository environment, or a list
with fewer than two returns `409 environment_repo_edit_blocked`.

When the environment reads its configuration from a repository
file (`repoFile` on GET /v1/environments/{id}), the file stays the
configuration source. The list must keep the `repoFile.url`
repository, or the request returns `409 repo_file_repo_removed`.
Repositories are compared by identity, so a trailing `.git` or
slash, a missing scheme, a leading `www.`, or GitHub letter case
still match. When the list names that repository in several forms,
the first entry is kept and the others dropped. For Bitbucket
Server, send the URL GET returns. An environment whose
only repository holds its configuration file returns
`409 repo_file_environment_locked` for any `repos`. Stored
repositories Cursor can't read return
`400 stored_repos_unreadable`.
